newsitem.title: JAPAN: Brazil's Kandir sees '97 trade deficit at $11 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Kandir sees '97 trade deficit at $11 bln.

text.p: Brazilian Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said on Wednesday his country sees a possible trade deficit of about $11 billion for calendar 1997.

Kandir said Brazil is aiming to increase exports by ensuring competitiveness of its products through investing in infrastructure, aggressive privatisation programs, alterations in the tax system, among other measures.
"Trade balance figures are being stimulated by imports, but these imports mainly consist of machinery and equipment," Kandir told a group of businessmen in Tokyo.
Investment in imported machinery and equipment is a good sign when seen from a long-term perspective, he added.

A recent restriction of credit card purchases abroad by prohibiting them to be financed and allowing foreign investor participation in Brazil's derivatives market are some of the subtle measures the country is taking to help narrow Brazil's current account gap, he said.

"If you look for each one of these measures it's impossible to say this would solve the problem, but if you put all these measures together it can help a lot," Kandir told Reuters in an interview earlier on Wednesday.
Kandir added his country expects a fiscal deficit of less than 2.5 percent of GDP for calendar 1997, compared to 3.9 percent for the previous year.
Kandir arrived in Tokyo on Monday for a five day visit to meet with members of the Japanese government and the economic sector.

He said while in Japan, he would sign loan contracts totalling $828 million to finance the construction of a highway which would be part of South America's Mercosur customs union, a sanitation program in the city of Salvador in northern Brazil, and business activities of a group of small and medium sized companies.
Members of the Mercosur include Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay.
